## Analysis at each round
### Round 1
There are no results in this search yet. In earlier searches, all 84 trials scored 0 on both dev and training success, so the agent never finishes an exact build. That points to optimisation and inductive bias, not generalisation. Several things must all be learned at once: placing bricks precisely, avoiding sealed cells, and choosing DONE at the right time. Reward is dense but forgives partly wrong bricks. Exactness depends mostly on the +1 final bonus, which favours a higher gamma. The six candidates below differ substantially and each combines several untested fixes: orthogonal init with small-gain logits, GroupNorm, a raw-observation skip into the footprint head, a learned max-pooled detector for DONE, factorised logits, a type-shared head, and a learned per-cell softmax over layers. The recipes span the untested extremes: lr 3e-3, gamma 0.995 with lambda 0.99, clip 0.3, rollout 64 with 1 epoch, and higher gamma generally. Compute stays at r ≤ about 1.2. If every candidate scores 0 again, the hidden world change is probably the obstacle.

### Round 2
All six round-1 trials scored 0 on dev and 0 on training success. That makes 90 of 90 trials at 0 across both searches. Initialisation hygiene, GroupNorm, LayerNorm, raw skips, factorised logits, learned layer-gathers, the recipe extremes and the spatial-free nets all failed. Because training success is also 0, the agent never finishes an exact build at all. That points to optimisation or a broken assumption, not to generalisation. Several failed nets could already represent the correctness rule (max, min and avg pooling of learned height and missing-layer features), so either learning is too slow or the unstated world change breaks an assumption. Round 2 therefore spreads its bets across six directions: (1) a new head that softly reads per-layer features at the learned landing layer over the footprint; (2) a head that adds structured, free local and dense terms, so it still works if the action layout differs; (3) a myopic wide per-cell MLP; (4) a deep depthwise trunk with a large-batch, long-horizon, conservative recipe; (5) an everything-plausible stack; (6) a spatial-free soft-landing net trained on more samples.

### Round 3
All 12 trials in this search scored 0 on dev and 0 on training success, as did all 84 trials in earlier searches. So the agent never finishes an exact build, even during training. That held for 188k to 426k samples, for soft landing-layer gathers, for layout-robust dense and 3x3 heads, for myopic and long-horizon recipes, and for GroupNorm with near-uniform initialisation. No idea has any evidence for it yet.

Three changes have not been combined with a structured head:
- the legality mask and coordinates as learned inputs, plus a per-action bias, which stay aligned with action indices even if the layout differs;
- how DONE is decided: hierarchical logits that split DONE, type and anchor, and a DONE head that reads the best placement score;
- per-cell checks inside the footprint, conditioned on footprint context and combined with a min, so the head can test that every covered cell is correct.

This round gives each of these its own candidate and adds a U-Net, a big-minibatch 3-epoch recipe and an "everything plausible" stack.

### Round 4
After 18 trials, every dev score and every training-success score is exactly 0. That matches the 84 zeros from earlier searches. Training success is also 0, so the agent never finishes an exact build even when sampling actions. The bottleneck is optimisation or inductive bias, not generalisation. Nothing tried so far has made any difference, including:
- soft landing-layer gathers;
- per-cell checks;
- hierarchical logits and a DONE head that reads the best placement;
- layout-robust dense and 3x3 heads;
- mask and coordinate inputs;
- U-Net context;
- recipe extremes such as myopic gamma, exploration and big batches.

This is the last round, so I am spreading the bets. Four ideas are new here:
- a concatenated-window footprint head that keeps each covered cell's learned features separately instead of only max, min and mean;
- a learned logit temperature, so the near-uniform starting policy can sharpen;
- attention-pooled global context;
- trading samples for capacity.

These are combined with untried recipes: 1024-sample minibatches at lr 3e-3, and ent 0 with lr 3e-3 at gamma 0.9. If all six score 0 again, the starting architecture stays selected.
